title: Engineering knowledge for your next task
description: Turn reviewed lessons, rules and acceptance criteria into focused instructions for coding agents.
text: The core workflow  CoFlow captures engineering knowledge, puts proposed changes through review, and compiles approved guidance for a specific task. Each package keeps its selection reasons and pinned dependencies, so recorded outcomes refer to the exact instructions delivered.   Capture a lesson or propose a rule with evidence.  Review its scope, exceptions and required checks.  Compile instructions using the task, repository, affected files and technologies.  Complete the work using your coding tools and record the outcome.     Explore the platform    Start with one task  Go from an approved rule to an instruction package.    Security and RLS  Understand tenant isolation and application security guidance.    Workflow Studio  Capture prototypes, review state graphs and export checks.    Measure outcomes  Read evidence, denominators and token budgets correctly.      Access and availability  These guides describe features implemented in the engineering-memory source. Hosted access, organization provisioning, feature flags and provider configuration determine what is available in your workspace. Documentation publication does not activate an application feature.   Request pilot access  or read the  feature availability guide .

title: Your first useful instruction package
description: Start with one repository, one engineering lesson and one task.

title: Rules, lessons and human review
description: Keep guidance scoped, evidence-backed and versioned.
text: Engineering rules registry  Rules include applicability, exceptions, priority, evidence and links to versioned skills or evaluations. Applicability can use project, repository, file paths, task type and technology. The effective rule is the latest approved revision; a pending draft does not silently replace it.    Review and revisions  Proposals enter a review workflow. Authorized reviewers approve, reject or request changes. Corrections create new revisions rather than rewriting approved history. When your workspace signs in with single sign-on, the person who wrote a rule cannot also approve it. A second verified teammate has to sign off.    Distillation and improvement proposals  CoFlow can group approved observations and propose improvements. The documented distillation path uses deterministic grouping and templates; it is not unrestricted semantic synthesis. The improvement heartbeat analyzes configured project outcomes and creates review candidates. It never approves its own suggestions.    Rules for RLS-sensitive application work  Capture requirements for tenant identity, authorized project scope, protected writes and pooled connections as project rules. Link positive and negative acceptance checks. CoFlow supplies reviewed guidance; your application, database policies and test runner enforce and verify the behavior.   Read the RLS guide .

title: Task-specific instructions
description: Select approved guidance with explicit reasons, dependency pins and budget checks.
text: How selection works  Start with the task and explicit file, repository and technology inputs. Applicability categories must match; entries within a category are alternatives. Approved exceptions can exclude a rule. Selection reasons help you inspect why guidance was included or excluded.    What a package contains  A persisted package can include approved rules, pinned skills, required evaluations, visual references and supporting lessons. Reopen it through  GET /v1/instructions/{id} . Historical reads preserve the original package rather than reconstructing it from today’s rules.    Token efficiency  Budget checks keep optional context bounded. Required guidance is not silently dropped to fit a budget. Instruction-size accounting uses a conservative UTF-8 byte upper bound, not an exact tokenizer measurement. Measure actual model input/output tokens and retries separately when assessing savings.    When compilation blocks  Declared conflicts, missing approved dependencies or required instructions that exceed the allowed budget can produce a blocked package. Resolve the underlying rule or dependency issue and compile again. Arbitrary contradictions in natural-language rules are not automatically detected.

title: Row-level security (RLS) and tenant isolation
description: Two separate concerns: protecting CoFlow data and guiding RLS-sensitive application changes.
text: RLS inside CoFlow  The PostgreSQL tenant implementation uses forced row-level security on protected tables, with organization ownership and server-resolved project scope. Application authorization checks also apply. Organization isolation alone does not grant access to every project.  Verified identity establishes transaction-local  app.organization_id  and  app.authorized_projects . Caller-supplied tenant headers are not an authorization source. Organization context without authorized project scope exposes no project records under the project-aware policies.    Runtime requirements   Use a restricted application role that does not own protected tables, is not a superuser, and cannot bypass RLS.  Backfill existing rows to verified organization/project ownership before activation.  Apply reviewed migrations through a separate authorized migration role.  Set transaction-local context for API, MCP and worker database operations, including after commits.  Verify missing-context denial, cross-tenant read/write denial and pooled-connection reuse against PostgreSQL.   SQLite development tests do not prove PostgreSQL RLS behavior. Startup guards check schema and role requirements; behavioral isolation tests remain necessary.    RLS in applications built with CoFlow  Use CoFlow to give coding agents approved RLS requirements before they change a protected route, migration or background job. Add an acceptance contract that covers both allowed and denied behavior.   Example rule: tenant-scoped invoice access  Resolve the organization from verified identity. Set its context in the query transaction. Require project authorization. Never treat possession of an invoice ID as permission.   This is engineering guidance for your implementation. CoFlow does not install, enable or certify RLS policies in your application merely because a rule is approved.    A useful acceptance checklist   Tenant A can read and update its own authorized records.  Tenant B cannot read, update, insert into or delete Tenant A’s records.  Missing organization or project scope fails closed.  Connection reuse does not retain another tenant’s context.  Workers and evaluations use the same authorization boundaries as API requests.  Cache, search and vocabulary results remain tenant and project scoped.   Source includes dedicated PostgreSQL RLS tests, including Workflow Studio isolation with a restricted non-bypass role. Confirm the evidence for the exact release deployed to your environment.

title: Organizations, projects and permissions
description: Control access through verified membership, role permissions and project assignments.
text: Membership and sign-in  CoFlow signs people in through your identity provider with single sign-on and keeps their access in step with their membership there. Local suspension and project permissions remain authoritative. Organization switching remounts the workspace in the new verified context.    Roles and project access  Built-in role templates include owner, admin, maintainer, contributor and viewer. Owners can manage organization-specific policies and custom roles. Direct project roles intersect with organization permissions; team assignments cannot elevate the organization role. Archived or deleted projects do not grant access.    Approval and audit  Knowledge read, capture and review are separate permissions. Sensitive changes append audit records. With single sign-on turned on, authors cannot approve their own knowledge. A second teammate reviews it. Last-owner protections help prevent administrative lockout.    Before inviting users  Confirm the deployed schema, restricted database role, single sign-on configuration, first owner and project assignments. Test with two organizations, including access revocation and cross-tenant denial. Availability depends on the deployed release and configured identity flow.

title: Workflow Studio
description: Turn self-contained HTML prototypes into reviewed, editable workflow evidence.
text: Upload and capture  Upload self-contained HTML pages and select an entry page. Playback uses an opaque-origin sandbox. Record interactions, form validation, error states and in-bundle navigation. Captures are validated and converted into workflow state graphs.    Edit, review and link  Relabel and annotate states or transitions, and add clearly marked manual steps. Each save creates an immutable revision. Authorized reviewers approve or reject revisions. Links to requirements and bugs pin the workflow revision, capture and source provenance.    Replay and export checks  Replay the trace and compare settled states. Export a Playwright test using stable locators where available. Unstable selectors are flagged with suggested test IDs. Unreviewed exports carry a warning; review them before adding them to monitoring.    Evidence and isolation  Replay results are client-reported, not independent server verification. Uploaded HTML is untrusted and cannot run in the application origin. The sandbox blocks many external interactions, but it is not a fully network-isolated server-side browser. Use synthetic input and avoid entering secrets into prototypes.  Workflow records use organization ownership, project authorization and forced PostgreSQL RLS.  Read the isolation guide .

title: Acceptance checks and outcome metrics
description: Measure what happened without confusing reported outcomes with independent verification.
text: Acceptance contracts  Specifications capture requirements, positive/negative checks and source references in immutable revisions. Approval checks the expected revision and digest, with a different recorded principal. Compile an approved specification with a code SHA to bind the acceptance contract into the instruction package.    Execution and evidence  Required checks run in your development or verification environment. Clients submit pass, fail or skipped results with evidence. Skipped checks do not count as passes. Freshness checks bind current specification/package/code references; they are not evidence that tests were independently executed.    Metrics you can inspect   Ready and blocked instruction packages, feedback coverage and reported outcomes.  Per-revision rule deliveries and reported violations.  Retrieval recall and reciprocal rank for approved evaluation sets.  Instruction budget estimates, measured separately from provider token usage.   Feedback coverage uses ready packages as its denominator. Reported success rates use recorded outcomes and remain empty when none exist. Source windows and bounded datasets must remain visible when interpreting dashboard totals.    Measure your pilot  Compare similar tasks using the same model and acceptance criteria. Track actual total tokens, review rounds, repeat findings and time to an accepted change. These pilot measurements do not establish a universal savings or compliance percentage.   Plan a pilot .

title: Coding agents, MCP and source connections
description: Connect reviewed engineering context without assuming every adapter is enabled.
text: Local MCP  The checked-in CoFlow MCP server runs over stdio and delegates calls to the authenticated API. Core tools include  compile_instructions ,  record_outcome ,  get_context ,  capture_memory  and  export_workspace . Approval remains a separate authorized API/UI workflow.  Use the installed  python -m app.mcp_server  entry point, your provisioned  MEMORY_API_URL  and an authorized  MEMORY_API_TOKEN  supplied through your local secure environment. Never paste credential values into repository configuration.    Agent instructions and exports  Approved workspace exports return AGENTS.md and MEMORY.md content without writing files on your machine. Review and place the exports in the workspace your agent reads. Local MCP compatibility depends on the client’s ability to launch a stdio server and use your approved configuration.    GitHub and Jira  The integration implementation includes organization-owned GitHub/Jira connection flows through Nango. GitHub capture uses an allowlisted repository and creates pending knowledge for review. Source-sync jobs require configured queues/workers and recheck authorization. Jira connection authorization does not imply issue synchronization is available.    MCP configuration catalog  The catalog versions, validates, reviews and audits MCP server descriptors. An approved descriptor starts disabled, and enablement requires a separate reviewed flag. Catalog records do not launch processes, connect to external servers or resolve secrets.    Availability limits  Do not use a sample hosted MCP URL as proof of a live CoFlow service. The stdio server in source is distinct from a remote HTTP/OAuth connector. Account provisioning, provider adapters and runtime flags must be verified for the release you use.

title: Feature availability
description: Implementation, configuration and live availability are different states.
text: Implemented in source  The guides cover rules and reviewed revisions, task compilation, package-linked outcomes, organization/project access, PostgreSQL RLS, Workflow Studio, specifications and acceptance contracts, knowledge search and source connection workflows.  This documentation was reviewed against source revision  6d7ba3d . Source implementation is not a claim that every workspace has been deployed or configured with it.    Configuration and rollout gates  Turning on single sign-on for a workspace requires verified membership, ownership backfill, policy coverage and a restricted runtime role. Workflow Studio, MCP catalogs, agent lifecycle/activity and source jobs have feature/configuration gates. Semantic retrieval/provider features have separate activation and budget requirements.    Boundaries to preserve   Agent lifecycle/activity records do not prove native provider discovery or execute coding agents.  Workflow replays and submitted acceptance reports are client-reported unless independently verified elsewhere.  MCP catalog approval does not connect a remote server.  Rule approval does not install RLS in another application.  Token budgets are not a published savings benchmark.     Confirm your workspace  Ask for the deployed version, enabled modules, sign-in URL and authorized projects during onboarding. Use account-specific application status and release evidence rather than marketing examples to decide what is live.

title: Troubleshooting
description: Start with the boundary that is blocking the workflow.
text: I can sign in but cannot open a project  Have an administrator check active local membership, current provider membership, project assignment and project status. Provider login is not enough. Do not work around the issue by adding a tenant ID to a request header.    Compilation is blocked  Read the blocker and selection reasons. Check approved rule revisions, declared conflict groups, pinned dependency status and required instruction size. Resolve the source issue and compile a new package; historical packages remain immutable.    Rows disappear after enabling RLS  Confirm ownership backfill and transaction-local organization plus authorized project scope. Use the correct restricted runtime role. Verify PostgreSQL behavior in a disposable environment before rollout; do not disable production policies to make a query return rows.    An integration or module is unavailable  Check that the exact deployed release contains the feature, its flags are enabled, and the provider/worker configuration is complete. A stored connection or catalog entry alone does not prove an adapter is active.    Ask for help  Send the module, safe error code, approximate time and deployed version to  support@getcoflow.ai . Share package IDs only through an approved support channel. Do not include tokens, personal data or private source content.

title: Plans, credits and prepaid usage
description: Included credits, prepaid top-ups, Business SSO and SOC 2 audit support.
text: Documentation / Plans and usage  Plans, credits and prepaid usage  Understand included credits, Business security features and usage expansion.   Monthly allowance  The proposed Team and Business offers each include approximately 1,000 credits per month. Credits cover supported CoFlow evaluations, automatic lesson generation and code scans. Lesson generation produces review candidates; it does not approve its own guidance.  Credit allowance scope, reset timing, expiry and rollover terms must be confirmed during onboarding. Do not assume 1,000 operations or 1,000 credits per agent or seat.    Prepaid top-ups  Additional usage is intended to use prepaid credit top-ups. Credit consumption reflects the selected workload, model and input/output token usage. Agent count helps plan demand; it is not itself a published credit conversion rate.  Credit-pack prices and operation weights have not been published. The public website prepares enquiries; it does not sell or activate top-ups. Confirm rates, funding arrangements and spending controls before purchasing.    Business security  Business includes single sign-on (SSO) and SOC 2 Type II audit support as part of the commercial offer. SSO requires provisioned identity configuration and the appropriate deployed release. Audit support covers readiness and evidence workflows; these docs do not assert an issued SOC 2 Type II report.   Visit the Trust Center  for the current access documentation, or read  RLS and tenant isolation .    Billing implementation and activation  The source includes versioned catalogs, usage events, entitlement checks, operation deduplication and separate model input/output token meters. Measured usage is distinct from charged usage. These foundations do not mean that the new 1,000-credit offer, conversion rates or top-up purchases have been activated.  Production billing needs a configured catalog and provider, approved prices/allowances and verified release controls. This website update changes the offer language, not the application’s billing configuration.    Plan your usage budget   Estimate monthly evaluations, lesson-generation jobs and code scans.  Identify the agents/models used and their expected input/output tokens.  Apply the published credit rate for each workload once available.  Choose prepaid capacity and confirm the spending limit before running additional paid work.    Discuss a credit package .   Updated November 20, 2026 ·  View pricing
